title: wktest-promote dated history

2026-07-15: delegated the FORCE=1 promote execution itself to Haiku (not just prep steps) since it is a pre-decided, reversible, backed-up operation -- distinguishes from destructive-guard-dodge delegation the user corrected earlier.

MEASUREMENT 2026-08-29 that RECONCILES step 10 rather than contradicting it, and the reconciliation is the useful part. Step 10 records bin/wkappbot.exe sitting EIGHT DAYS STALE while the smoke suite exercised only the core. Today the opposite was measured: immediately after bash bin/wktest-build.sh, bin/wkappbot.exe and bin/wktest-appbot.exe were BYTE-IDENTICAL -- both 7230464 bytes, both stamped 00:21, sha256 58bf0ceb79ca5e6c5e8929023718f3363d94adab492f8be7b09c8fb71fdbc944 -- while the build printed LAUNCHER staged as wktest-appbot.exe NOT deployed and deferred the launcher smoke to this script. CORRECTED SAME SESSION, TWICE, AND THE SECOND CORRECTION IS THE HONEST ONE: I do NOT know what wrote bin/wkappbot.exe. I first asserted the build deploys it, then invented a rebuilt-project condition to reconcile step 10, and only then READ the script -- bin/wktest-build.sh line 128 records that the cp onto the canonical name was DELIBERATELY REMOVED, line 146 writes wktest-appbot.exe alone, and line 143 says wktest-promote.sh copies that same file onto wkappbot.exe only when the smoke passes. So the printed message appears TRUE and my two explanations were both fabricated to fit a measurement. Nor is it a hardlink: ls -li gives different inodes, 3458764513916733333 against 3458764513916401557. WHAT IS MEASURED stands -- two separate files, identical 7230464 bytes, identical sha256, identical 00:21 timestamp, right after a build that says it deployed nothing. WHAT IS UNKNOWN is the writer, and no promote script was run by this session. WHEN: before any claim about launcher freshness, and before designing any before-and-after launcher comparison. HOW: sha256sum bin/wkappbot.exe bin/wktest-appbot.exe right after a build, and copy the live launcher aside BEFORE building if a real baseline is needed -- run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto for why the comparison must be against an independently captured artifact rather than against the thing you just produced. WHY IT COST REAL TIME: three probe designs were spent comparing old launcher against new to verify an Eye-pipe routing change, and both names resolved to the same bytes, so identical outputs were read as evidence about routing when they were evidence of nothing. That is step 10's own lesson arriving from the other side -- a check, or a probe, that cannot fail for the real reason is not measuring what its author believes.
